skill.name: tasknotes
skill.description: Manage Obsidian TaskNotes through its local API, including task listing, filtering, creation, updates, deletion, statistics, and configuration discovery.
skill.summary: Manage Obsidian tasks through the local TaskNotes API.
skill.author: ArtemXTech

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, placeholders, or intended requests to the local TaskNotes API. Semantic review found unvalidated URL construction, optional authentication, and deletion without confirmation. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: TASKNOTES_API_PORT can alter the request authority and redirect bearer credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Accept only integer ports from 1 through 65535, keep the hostname fixed, and send authorization only to the expected origin.

remediation.issue: Task creation, updates, and deletion can use an unauthenticated local API.
remediation.suggestion: Require a TaskNotes token for mutation commands and recommend authenticated API configuration in the setup guide.

remediation.issue: The delete command performs a destructive request without confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Add an interactive confirmation and a separate explicit flag for approved noninteractive deletion.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated port value can redirect authenticated requests
semantic_findings.description: TASKNOTES_API_PORT enters the URL authority without numeric validation. A crafted value can change the destination and expose the bearer token.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The port value flows directly into the URL authority, while the API key becomes a bearer header. No validation restricts the port to digits.

semantic_findings.title: Task mutation API can operate without authentication
semantic_findings.description: The setup permits an empty API token, and the client then omits authorization. Other local processes could modify or delete TaskNotes data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly permits an empty token, and the client omits Authorization when absent. This behavior is direct and unambiguous.

semantic_findings.title: Delete command has no confirmation safeguard
semantic_findings.description: The CLI sends a DELETE request immediately for the supplied task identifier. An agent mistake can cause unintended task loss without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The delete command directly issues DELETE after argument parsing. No confirmation flag or prompt exists in the complete CLI implementation.

content.value_statement: Manual TaskNotes maintenance can slow daily planning. This skill uses the local API to list, create, update, and delete Obsidian tasks.
actual_capabilities: List tasks with status, project, priority, overdue, and result-limit filters.
Create tasks with projects, priorities, dates, contexts, time estimates, and details.
Update task titles, statuses, priorities, dates, and descriptions.
Delete tasks by TaskNotes file identifier.
Display task statistics and configured filter options.
Return readable tables or structured output for agent workflows.
limitations: Requires Obsidian, the TaskNotes plugin, and its HTTP API to be running locally.
Supports only the fields and commands implemented by the included CLI.
Uses configured status and priority values without validating them before requests.
Does not provide interactive confirmation before task updates or deletion.

use_cases.title: Plan a personal workday
use_cases.description: Review active and overdue tasks, then identify the next items by priority and due date.

use_cases.title: Maintain project tasks
use_cases.description: Create project-linked tasks and update their status as work progresses.

use_cases.title: Automate task workflows
use_cases.description: Use structured task results to support agent-driven planning and reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Review current tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Show my current TaskNotes tasks in a readable table.

prompt_templates.title: Create a project task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TaskNotes task titled [title], linked to [project], with priority [priority] and due date [date].

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize overdue work
prompt_templates.prompt: List up to five overdue tasks for [project], then summarize them by priority and due date.

prompt_templates.title: Review and update a project
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect available TaskNotes options, find active tasks for [project], propose status changes, and ask before applying any update.

output_examples.output: Three in-progress tasks found. The table includes status, priority, title, and project for each task.

output_examples.input: Create a high-priority task named Prepare launch notes for the Website project.
output_examples.output: Created 'Prepare launch notes' with high priority and linked it to the Website project.

output_examples.input: What statuses and priorities are available?
output_examples.output: Available statuses and priorities are listed from the current TaskNotes configuration.

best_practices: Enable a TaskNotes API token before allowing automated task changes.
Run the options command before using status or priority values from a new vault.
Review task identifiers and proposed changes before update or delete operations.
anti_patterns: Do not place unrelated secrets in the vault environment file.
Do not expose the TaskNotes API port beyond the local machine.
Do not delete tasks from ambiguous natural-language references.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Obsidian, the TaskNotes plugin, and the plugin HTTP API enabled on the local machine.

faq.question: Is an API token required?
faq.answer: The client supports token-free access, but a TaskNotes API token is recommended for task changes.

faq.question: Which task fields can it change?
faq.answer: It can change titles, statuses, priorities, due dates, scheduled dates, and details.

faq.question: Can it filter task lists?
faq.answer: Yes. It filters by status, project, priority, overdue state, and result limit.

faq.question: Does task data stay local?
faq.answer: The CLI targets localhost. Task content can still pass through the active AI tool when prompts or responses include it.

faq.question: Can the CLI undo a deleted task?
faq.answer: The CLI offers no undo command. Use Obsidian or TaskNotes recovery features when available.
